- When sentiment is strongly negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast peak and introduce early downward slope.
- If sentiment turns positive (avg > -0.1) mid-horizon, model frequently underreacts; adjust forecast to show gradual upward trend, not flat or downward.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is volatile; add 2–3% upward bias to early forecast points.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly negative (avg -0.1 to 0.0), model often overpredicts mean reversion; delay downward correction until later horizon (e.g., day 10+).
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (avg > 0.1) and price is trending up, model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope and avoid premature flattening.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment volatility in early horizon; if sentiment swings sharply within 3–5 days, adjust forecast to reflect volatility (e.g., ±2–3% band around mean).
